test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - Numerical Ability (Held on: 02 Dec, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: Bhumika deposited Rs. 8,000, which amounted to Rs. 9,200 after 3 years at r% p.a. simple interest. Had the interest rate been 2% more, that is, (r + 2)% per annum, what amount would she have received?
solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 8,000

Amount (A) = Rs. 9,200

Time (T) = 3 years

Rate of interest (r) = ?

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × r × T) / 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

**Calculation:**

Simple Interest (SI) = A - P

⇒ SI = 9,200 - 8,000

⇒ SI = 1,200

Using SI formula:

⇒ 1,200 = (8,000 × r × 3) / 100

⇒ 1,200 = 24,000r / 100

⇒ 1,200 = 240r

⇒ r = 1,200 / 240

⇒ r = 5%

New rate of interest = r + 2% = 5% + 2% = 7%

New Simple Interest (SI) = (P × new rate × T) / 100

⇒ New SI = (8,000 × 7 × 3) / 100

⇒ New SI = 168,000 / 100

⇒ New SI = 1,680

New Amount = P + New SI

⇒ New Amount = 8,000 + 1,680

⇒ New Amount = 9,680

**The amount Bhumika would have received is Rs. 9,680.**
